title: Learning From the Competition Can Make You Better
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This article encourages leaders to treat competitors as a source of insight rather than just comparison, citing Ford CEO Jim Farley's admission that dismantling a Tesla Model 3 and Chinese EVs forced Ford to rethink its manufacturing approach. The recommended process is deconstruction — examining the steps and decisions a competitor made using frameworks like SWOT or Value Chain Analysis — followed by asking what insights can genuinely be applied to your own thinking. The piece's central distinction is between comparison, which it says leads organizations astray, and understanding why competitors do what they do, which enables real differentiation and innovation.
points: Ford CEO Jim Farley was "humbled" after engineers dismantled a Tesla Model 3 and Chinese EVs, forcing a rethink of Ford's manufacturing.
Deconstructing a competitor's product or service — using tools like SWOT or Value Chain Analysis — surfaces insights, not just comparisons.
Analyzing competitor missteps helps a team avoid similar mistakes.
Understanding why a competitor does something is more valuable than simply comparing outcomes to it.
quotes: Competitors can be a source of learning, growth, and inspiration — if leaders let them be.
CEO Jim Farley admitted that he was “humbled” after engineers tore apart a Tesla Model 3 and several Chinese electric vehicles in 2022.
Ford learned it had to catch up to its competitors so the company could compete in the future.
It is less important to learn what the competitor is doing and more important to understand why .
The best leaders refrain from comparison and focus on learning instead.
